editor_note:
The dominant thread this run is commitment: pharma and enterprise incumbents are no longer piloting AI — they're funding it as core infrastructure. Sanofi's $294M Toronto hub and SAP's $1.16B acquisition of Prior Labs in the same cycle signal a shift from strategy decks to capital deployed at scale. Recursion's CEO transition tells the same story from the inside: the AI drug-discovery space is correcting from hype to execution discipline, and Najat Khan's reset is a candid benchmark for what serious AI-in-pharma looks like right now.

On the capabilities side, Latent Space's physics episode is the strongest AI-for-science signal in months — GPT-5.x producing novel results in quantum gravity moves the needle on what foundation models can do in research workflows. OpenAI's B2B Signals report quantifies the enterprise implementation gap that everyone in this seat feels. The Services framing from Latent Space names the strategic shift cleanly: as models commoditize, managed services become the new moat, and that has direct implications for vendor strategy. The Pennsylvania Character.AI lawsuit closes the loop — liability precedent from a chatbot impersonating a psychiatrist belongs on your governance radar before your own deployments scale.
